title: Do Cells Work as a Team? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A crowd, a team and a machine: Aarav asks whether the cells inside an animal work like a crowd, a team or a machine. Every animal is made of many cells, but the cells are not organised in the same way.

You will see the four levels of organisation from NCERT: cellular (sponges), tissue (coelenterates like Hydra), organ (flatworms) and organ system (annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates). A zoom ladder goes from a sponge to its body wall and one collar cell, showing division of labour. Then the two body systems exams compare: an incomplete gut with one opening versus a complete gut with a mouth and an anus, and open versus closed circulation, both animated. A worked example places four animals on the levels, followed by the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 32 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
